title: Half-plane convergence
statement:
Let $(D,E_2,\alpha,f,g)$ be the exact couple of
[def-sp-exact-couple]. Assume $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<a$, and $E_2^{p,q}=0$ unless
$p\geq0$ and $q\geq a$. Put $A^n=D^{0,n}$. Then total degree $n$ contains
only $a\leq q\leq n$, and each entry $E_r^{p,q}$ has stabilized when

$$
 r>\max(q-a+1,\,p),
$$

with the canonical identification $E_r^{p,q}=E_{r+1}^{p,q}$ supplied by page
cohomology. For $q\leq n$, set
$G_qA^n=\operatorname{im}(D^{n-q,q}\xrightarrow{\alpha^{n-q}}A^n)$, and set
$G_qA^n=A^n$ for $q\geq n$. The decreasing filtration
[def-sp-filtration] $F^pA^n=G_{n-p}A^n$ is finite, exhaustive and separated,
and $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong F^pA^{p+q}/F^{p+1}A^{p+q}$. The couple is regular
and complete in the sense of [def-sp-convergence].

proof.text: Induct on pages: a zero E entry has zero kernel and subsequent cokernel. The half-plane region persists. If r+2 exceeds both bounds, the incoming source and outgoing target vanish. The kernel inclusion and cokernel projection are isomorphisms; their composite gives the canonical stabilization. The cycle and boundary recurrences are then stationary. Monotonicity makes the stationary values their greatest lower and least upper bounds, constructing L and proving regularity.

Use normalized diagonal colimits. Their nonpositive maps are isomorphisms, so the image filtration is top there. For p>n-a the cocone source D^{p,n-p} is zero, so the filtration step is bottom. These two steps prove finiteness, exhaustivity and separatedness. For completeness of the couple, an incoming iterate whose source second index lies below a has zero image, so every common lower bound is bottom.

Apply canonical weak convergence to L and the normalized colimits. The weakConvergence_comparison theorem of def-sp-convergence yields the associated-graded isomorphisms commuting with the two specified maps. Combined with regularity, separatedness and exhaustivity this proves abutting.

For inverse-limit completeness, use a zero filtration step m. All later steps are zero, so their cokernel projections are isomorphisms. Given a compatible quotient cone f, define h as f_m followed by the inverse projection. Integer induction upwards cancels invertible quotient transitions; downwards uses cone compatibility. Uniqueness follows by cancelling the projection at m. This proves convergence.

lean.statement: theorem halfPlaneConvergence (X : BigradedExactCouple C 0) (a : ℤ) (hD : ∀ (p q : ℤ), q < a → IsZero (X.D p q)) (hE : ∀ (p q : ℤ), (p < 0 ∨ q < a) → IsZero (X.E p q)) : ∃ L : LimitSubobjects X, ∃ A : ∀ n : ℤ, AlphaColimit X n, ∃ hA : ∀ n : ℤ, (A n).obj = X.D 0 n, (∀ n : ℤ, (A n).ι 0 ≫ eqToHom (hA n) = eqToHom (by congr 1; omega)) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (n p q : ℤ), p + q = n → ¬ IsZero ((X.pageCouple r).E p q) → a ≤ q ∧ q ≤ n) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), (r : ℤ) + 2 > max (q - a + 1) p → ∃ e : (X.pageCouple r).E p q ≅ (X.pageCouple (r + 1)).E p q, kernel.ι ((X.pageCouple r).d p q) ≫ e.hom = (X.pageCouple r).derivedEProjection p q) ∧ (∀ (n p : ℤ), p ≤ 0 → (X.imageFiltration n (A n)).step p = ⊤) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, (X.imageFiltration n (A n)).IsFinite ∧ (X.imageFiltration n (A n)).IsExhaustive ∧ (X.imageFiltration n (A n)).IsSeparated) ∧ (∀ (p q : ℤ), ∃ e : X.pageInfinity L p q ≅ (X.imageFiltration (p + q) (A (p + q))).gradedPiece p, X.toPageInfinity L p q ≫ e.hom = X.toGradedPiece A p q) ∧ X.IsComplete ∧ X.ConvergesTo L A
